title: Agartala Conspiracy Case
subtitle: A state prosecution that intensified nationalist mobilization in East Pakistan.
summary: In 1968, the Pakistan government prosecuted Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and others in the Agartala Conspiracy Case, alleging plans to separate East Pakistan with Indian support. The case became a flashpoint of political anger, expanded solidarity across student and public spheres, and directly fed into the 1969 mass uprising.
heroTagline: The 1968 trial transformed legal prosecution into mass political resistance.
whyItMatters: The Agartala case matters because it exposed the legitimacy crisis of centralized rule and helped convert constitutional autonomy politics into a mass anti-authoritarian movement.
longTermLegacy: The Agartala case matters because it exposed the legitimacy crisis of centralized rule and helped convert constitutional autonomy politics into a mass anti-authoritarian movement.
